properties: Instance-qualified opaque IDs; complete-list absence only; reset and evidence fences; event payloads never publish; declared verbs and acquisition limits; retired and disabled owners cannot acquire or publish; synthetic code excluded from the production bundle
assessment: One provider-neutral admission suite exercised by native Herdr fixtures and a deterministic paginated terminal-less source, with malformed-source controls, production-entrypoint bundling and an opt-in disposable Herdr session
remaining: Durable World binding resolution, cross-source claim display rules and legacy verb policy belong to later identity/verb work. Synthetic subscription crossing remains a named pending v2 gate. Live Herdr evidence requires HERDR_WORLD_LIVE_ADAPTERS=1 and the installed Herdr binary.

partialEvidence.review: The accepted delivery link records the merged design contract, not implementation acceptance. This adapter implementation awaits independent PR review.

evidenceDecision: P3 selects direct external-source conformance rather than a finite model. Existing runtime/snapshot models remain required for their unchanged owner fences; these tests establish the new adapter boundary, not durable identity, effect recovery or v2 delivery. Typed runtime-port translation and actual raw-client-free snapshot, Desk screen and terminal-setting consumers add direct compatibility evidence; native traffic, lease ownership and no-replay behavior retain their existing contracts. Remaining callback areas are explicitly TUI-only; no core runtime is enabled. Mutation regressions exercise native write and float-shell lease refusal through a sibling runtime, and decisive foreground-pid and authorization checks. These extend direct core consumer conformance rather than the provider-neutral model domain.

promotion.scope: New adapter boundary only; independent implementation review and CI required.
